claims.text: A literal equation is an equation that has several letters or variables.
claims.quote: A literal equation is one that has several letters or variables.

claims.text: The area of a circle is an example of a literal equation: A = πr².
claims.quote: Examples include the area of a circle $\left(A=\pi{r}^{2}\right)$

claims.text: The formula for speed is an example of a literal equation: v = D/t.
claims.quote: the formula for speed $\left(v=\frac{D}{t}\right)$

claims.text: Solving literal equations is also known as changing the subject of the formula.
claims.quote: Solving literal equations is also known as changing the subject of the formula.

claims.text: Literal equations are solved in terms of one variable.
claims.quote: In this section we solve literal equations in terms of one variable.

claims.text: Solving literal equations uses the principles learnt about solving equations, applied to rearranging literal equations.
claims.quote: we use the principles we have learnt about solving equations and apply them to rearranging literal equations

claims.text: To isolate the unknown variable, ask "what is it joined to?" and "how is it joined?"
claims.quote: We isolate the unknown variable by asking “what is it joined to?” and “how is it joined?”

claims.text: After finding what the unknown variable is joined to and how, perform the opposite operation to both sides as a whole.
claims.quote: We then perform the opposite operation to both sides as a whole.

claims.text: If the unknown variable is in two or more terms, take it out as a common factor.
claims.quote: If the unknown variable is in two or more terms, then we take it out as a common factor.

claims.text: When the square root of both sides is taken, remember that there will be a positive and a negative answer.
claims.quote: If we have to take the square root of both sides, remember that there will be a positive and a negative answer.

claims.text: If the unknown variable is in the denominator, multiply both sides by the lowest common denominator (LCD) and then continue to solve.
claims.quote: If the unknown variable is in the denominator, we multiply both sides by the lowest common denominator (LCD) and then continue to solve.

claims.text: LCD is the abbreviation for lowest common denominator.
claims.quote: the lowest common denominator (LCD)

claims.text: The area of a triangle is A = ½bh.
claims.quote: The area of a triangle is $A=\frac{1}{2}bh$

claims.text: To isolate the required variable, rearrange the equation with that variable on one side of the equals sign and the rest of the variables on the other.
claims.quote: we must rearrange the equation with $h$ on one side of the equals sign and the rest of the variables on the other

claims.text: To make h the subject of A = ½bh, the book rearranges to 2A = bh and then to 2A/b = h.
claims.quote: A&=\frac{1}{2}bh\\2A&=bh\\\frac{2A}{b}&=h

claims.text: The height of a triangle is given by h = 2A/b.
claims.quote: The height of a triangle is given by: $h=\dfrac{2A}{b}$

claims.text: To make R the subject of h = R × H/(R + r²), the first step clears the denominator R + r² by multiplying both sides by it, giving h(R + r²) = R × H.
claims.quote: h\left(R+{r}^{2}\right)&=R\timesH

claims.text: After clearing the denominator, continue to solve by expanding the bracket: h(R + r²) becomes hR + hr², giving hR + hr² = HR.
claims.quote: hR+h{r}^{2}&=HR

claims.text: When R appears in more than one term, collect the terms containing R on one side: hr² = HR − hR.
claims.quote: h{r}^{2}&=HR-hR

claims.text: Take R out as a common factor of the terms on that side: hr² = R(H − h).
claims.quote: h{r}^{2}&=R\left(H-h\right)

claims.text: After factorising, dividing by (H − h) gives R = hr²/(H − h).
claims.quote: \therefore R&=\frac{h{r}^{2}}{H-h}

solution: Isolate the required variable: We are asked to isolate the height, so we must rearrange the equation with $h$ on one side of the equals sign and the rest of the variables on the other. $\begin{align*}A&=\frac{1}{2}bh\\2A&=bh\\\frac{2A}{b}&=h\end{align*}$
Write the final answer: The height of a triangle is given by: $h=\dfrac{2A}{b}$
